skill.name: extract-transcripts
skill.description: Extract readable markdown transcripts from Claude Code and Codex CLI JSONL session files.
skill.summary: Convert local AI coding session logs into readable transcripts and searchable indexes.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts for markdown backticks, option names, and schema identifiers are false positives. Confirmed risks are local command execution instructions, hidden Claude and Codex transcript access, persistent DuckDB indexing of transcript content, and user-selected output writes. No prompt injection or network exfiltration was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Sensitive transcript content is persisted in a local index.
remediation.suggestion: Add redaction options, document cleanup commands, and warn users before indexing default Claude or Codex session directories.

remediation.issue: Default commands access hidden session and history stores.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit path selection or confirmation before scanning hidden home-directory transcript locations.

remediation.issue: Transcript export can overwrite a user-specified file.
remediation.suggestion: Use exclusive file creation by default, add an overwrite flag, or warn when the output path already exists.

remediation.issue: Detailed exports can include tool inputs and thinking blocks.
remediation.suggestion: Keep detailed fields disabled by default and add warnings that generated transcripts may contain sensitive information.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Index Stores Full Transcript Content
semantic_findings.description: The indexer stores local session message content in a persistent DuckDB database without redaction or encryption. Claude and Codex transcripts may contain secrets, prompts, tool output, project paths, and repository metadata.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code defines hidden default session and database paths, extracts message content, and inserts that content into the messages table. This directly supports persistent local storage of sensitive transcript text.

semantic_findings.title: Detailed Exports Can Reveal Tool Inputs And Thinking
semantic_findings.description: The Claude extractor can include tool inputs and thinking blocks in generated markdown. Those fields can expose sensitive commands, arguments, file paths, or reasoning text when outputs are shared.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation advertises include-tools and include-thinking, and the code writes thinking blocks plus serialized tool input into markdown. Exposure depends on user flags, so the risk is medium rather than critical.

content.value_statement: AI coding session histories are difficult to review in raw JSONL form. This skill converts Claude Code and Codex sessions into readable markdown and searchable indexes.
actual_capabilities: Convert Claude Code JSONL sessions into markdown transcripts.
Convert Codex CLI session and history files into readable summaries.
Include tool calls and thinking blocks when selected.
Process one session file or all JSONL files in a directory.
Build a DuckDB index for recent, search, and show commands.
Filter indexed sessions by project name or time window.
limitations: Requires local access to Claude Code or Codex JSONL session files.
DuckDB indexing requires the duckdb Python package.
Codex extraction truncates very long messages.
Does not redact secrets from exported transcripts or indexes.

use_cases.title: Review a Debugging Session
use_cases.description: Convert a completed Claude Code session into markdown for later review and bug analysis.

use_cases.title: Create Project Notes
use_cases.description: Turn AI coding conversations into readable notes that explain decisions, commands, and outcomes.

use_cases.title: Search Local Session History
use_cases.description: Index past sessions and find conversations by keyword, project, or recent activity.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use extract-transcripts to convert this Claude Code session file into a readable markdown transcript: <session.jsonl>.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Session Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Use extract-transcripts on this session directory, process all JSONL files, skip empty sessions, and return summary output only.

prompt_templates.title: Export Detailed Transcript
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract this session with tool calls and thinking blocks included, then save the markdown output to a private review file.

prompt_templates.title: Index and Search Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the DuckDB transcript index, search for "error handling", filter to my project, and show the most relevant session summary.

output_examples.input: A Claude Code session JSONL file from a local project.
output_examples.output: A markdown transcript with session date, duration, model, working directory, user messages, and assistant responses.

output_examples.input: A Codex CLI history file containing several prompts.
output_examples.output: A dated list of Codex history entries with long prompts shortened for easier scanning.

output_examples.input: A transcript index search for error handling in one project.
output_examples.output: Recent matching sessions grouped by date, project, branch, file path, and matching message snippet.

best_practices: Review transcripts for secrets before sharing any output.
Use summary mode before exporting full conversations.
Store generated transcript files and indexes in private locations.
anti_patterns: Do not export all sessions into a shared folder without review.
Do not include thinking blocks unless they are required for analysis.
Do not index directories outside the intended session storage paths.

faq.question: What session formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude Code JSONL sessions, Codex CLI session JSONL files, and Codex history JSONL files.

faq.question: Does it upload transcripts anywhere?
faq.answer: No network upload code was found. The scripts read and write local files only.

faq.question: Can it process many sessions at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The Claude extractor can process all JSONL files in a directory, and the indexer can scan session folders.

faq.question: Where does the searchable index live?
faq.answer: By default, the DuckDB index is stored under the local Claude transcript index directory.

faq.question: Does it hide secrets in transcripts?
faq.answer: No. Users should review and redact secrets before sharing generated transcripts or index results.

faq.question: What dependency is needed for indexing?
faq.answer: The indexer requires the duckdb Python package. Basic transcript extraction uses the Python standard library.
